Title: Gazette confirms revocation of 10 Negri Sembilan exco appointments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The revocation of the appointments of 10 Negeri Sembilan executive council members has been gazetted today.
The revocation was made under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959, which provides that a state executive councillor, other than the menteri besar, holds office at the pleasure of the ruler, FMT reported.
"The state executive councillors had taken and signed their oaths and pledges of allegiance before Tuanku Muhriz on Aug 7, 2026, before assuming their positions.
"The appointments were revoked after the ten had breached their oaths of allegiance," read the document.
They are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
The revocation took effect on Sept 20.
The impasse between the Negri Sembilan palace and the administration has been ongoing since April, when the Undang Yang Empat proclaimed the removal of Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was reported to be among those who
signed the proclamation
, although he later claimed that he had done so under duress.
It was then reported that Tuanku Muhriz
revoked
the exco members' appointments over a breach of their oath.
Earlier today, Menteri Besar Datuk
Ismail Lasim
said the state executive councillors were barred from entering their offices in Wisma Negeri.

Title: IHH unit appeals RM5.3bil Japan claim ruling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd's subsidiary Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd (NTK) has appealed to the Tokyo High Court against a ruling dismissing its ¥200 billion (about RM5.3 billion) damages claim against Japanese pharmaceutical company Daiichi Sankyo Co Ltd.
The appeal follows the Tokyo District Court's Sept 10 dismissal of all claims brought by NTK and its order for the IHH unit to bear the litigation costs.
IHH said NTK concluded that the matter warranted review by a higher court after assessing the judgment and exercised its right of appeal.
"Having assessed the judgment, NTK concluded that it warrants appellate review by a higher court, and has accordingly exercised its right of appeal," IHH said in a statement today.
The dispute is linked to IHH's 2018 acquisition of a controlling stake in India's Fortis Healthcare Ltd, which subsequently became the subject of legal complications involving Daiichi Sankyo and the former Fortis promoters.
IHH, through NTK, bought a 31 per cent stake in Fortis, but later halted its open offer to acquire a further 26 per cent.
This was after Daiichi Sankyo filed contempt proceedings against the Indian hospital group's founders.
The legal dispute dates back to Daiichi Sankyo's separate battle with former Fortis promoters Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh.
Daiichi Sankyo had acquired Ranbaxy Laboratories from the Singh brothers in 2008 and subsequently alleged that the brothers had withheld information concerning regulatory issues at the Indian drugmaker.
A Singapore arbitration tribunal in 2016 ordered the brothers to pay Daiichi Sankyo about 25.62 billion Indian rupees in damages, plus interest.
The dispute subsequently spilled over into Fortis, which the Singh brothers controlled.
IHH emerged as a "white knight" in 2018, acquiring a controlling stake through NTK and triggering a mandatory open offer.
IHH has maintained that it suffered losses because of delays in obtaining the mandatory tender offer approvals needed for its Fortis acquisition.
It has also stressed that it was not a party to the dispute between Daiichi Sankyo and the judgment debtors.
NTK initially filed its lawsuit against Daiichi Sankyo in the Tokyo District Court in October 2023, seeking more than ¥20 billion in damages.
It later amended its claim in May 2025 to ¥203.3 billion, according to Daiichi Sankyo.
In its latest statement, IHH reiterated that the Fortis acquisition was undertaken through a transparent, publicly disclosed and fully regulated process.
The transaction received the required corporate, shareholder and regulatory approvals, including those under India's Competition Commission and Securities and Exchange Board of India regulations.
Meanwhile, the legal proceedings have not altered IHH's stated plans for Fortis and its wider India operations.
IHH said India remains a key strategic market and that it plans to increase its stake in Fortis to 51 per cent over the next three to five years, further integrate its Fortis and Gleneagles platforms and expand its capacity in India to about 10,000 beds by 2031.
"As one of the largest and longest-standing foreign direct investors in India's hospital sector, IHH has remained steadfast in its commitment to the country despite the challenges arising from this matter. ," it said.

Title: Global bond rout rolls on, pushes 30-year US Treasury yields to highest since 2004
Article:
LONDON: US 30-year borrowing costs hit their highest in over 20 years on Thursday, adding strain to the government's long-term finances, as investors upped the compensation they demand to hold bonds given strong economic growth and high energy prices.
The yield on the 30-year US Treasury climbed to just over 5.44 per cent, its highest since 2004, as prices fell.
Global bond yields jumped on Wednesday and Thursday after business activity data pointed to strong US growth and rising inflation pressures, stoking Federal Reserve rate-hike bets.
Global bond markets have been under pressure for months as the Iran war pushed up energy prices, growth has proved resilient and investors fret about high levels of government debt.
Yet investors have, so far, absorbed the rise in yields to multi-decade highs, given the resilience of underlying economic growth, booming corporate profits and the avalanche of spending particularly related funding the AI boom.
"Obviously the higher things go, the worse everything looks, and the more expensive US mortgages will be, for example, and the bigger the debt interest burden of the federal government," said Daiwa Capital's head of economic research Chris Scicluna.
"But for as long as it's orderly, it's not overly dramatic."
While shorter-dated Treasury yields track expectations for interest rates, the 30-year yield reflects investors' willingness to finance government borrowing in the years ahead.
Germany's finance agency said on Thursday it expects federal borrowing to hit a record €525.5 billion (US$598 billion) in 2026 and to rise further next year, driven largely by rising refinancing needs and growing requirements for special funds.
Japan's 10-year bond yield on Thursday hit its highest since 1996.
BROADER HIT
The cost to households has been immediate.
US 30-year mortgage rates are now a percentage point higher than they were before the war and, at 7 per cent, around their highest in two years.
But with nominal growth running at around 8 per cent in the second quarter and showing no signs of slowing materially, investors have remained sanguine.
New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said on Thursday the US economy was displaying "remarkable resilience".
"It's clearly evident in the PMI punch that we got yesterday which really showed capacity constraints with work backlogs going up and employment rising rapidly, fastest in five years, or four years.
"So this is putting pressure on prices and showing that the economy is growing," Hank Calenti, global markets strategist at SMBC EMEA, said.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has taken extraordinary measures to contain rising borrowing costs, including intervening to buy the yen to avoid officials in Tokyo selling Treasuries to do so, or expanding buybacks of 20- and 30-year debt, but to little avail.
The US already boasts some of the highest yields among the Group of Seven richest nations.
"Treasuries are competing with the rest of the market to be purchased and so you know the question is how much higher could it go?," Calenti said.

Title: Russia says will 'consider' US G20 invitation for Putin
Article:
MOSCOW: Russia said on Thursday it would consider an invitation from the US government for President Vladimir Putin to attend G20 summit in the United States in December.
President Donald Trump has invited Putin to attend the summit of world leaders in Miami, a move announced earlier this week by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio after his meeting with Russia's top diplomat Sergei Lavrov.
The move comes as Washington struggles to secure a deal to end the four-and-a-half-year war in Ukraine, with Trump insisting he is working with both sides.
"No decision has yet been taken" on whether Putin will travel to Miami for the summit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Thursday.
"We certainly receive this kind invitation with appreciation. We value this invitation. It will be considered... and a decision will then be made," Peskov added.
While the US and Russian presidents have spoken by telephone on various occasions, the last time they met was in 2025.
The G20 summit will take place on December 14-15 as the US holds the rotating presidency of the forum bringing together the world's major advanced and emerging economies.
Its members include France, Germany and Britain, all three prominent supporters of Ukraine as it fends off Russia's offensive launched by Moscow in February 2022.

Title: PMCK's Q1 earnings surge 245pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PMCK Bhd's net profit more than tripled in the first quarter of financial year 2027 (Q1 FY27).
This optimism stemmed from higher inpatient revenue, driven by improved admissions and bed occupancy.
The private healthcare services provider's net profit for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 rose 245 per cent to RM3.05 million from RM884,000 a year earlier.
Its revenue increased five per cent to RM22.90 million from RM21.76 million previously.
In a statement, PMCK managing director Datuk Lee Gaik Cheng said the company remains focused on disciplined execution and prudent investment as it looks ahead.
"We will continue to invest prudently in our capabilities, including the ongoing development of Putra Medical Centre Kulim (PMC Kulim), while maintaining a disciplined approach to cost management amid a challenging cost environment," she said.
PMCK remains cautiously optimistic about the private healthcare industry.
This is supported by continued demand for quality healthcare services and the company's efforts to strengthen its service capabilities and operational capacity.
"We will continue to focus on improving patient access, strengthening our service capabilities and enhancing operational efficiency, while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation as we pursue opportunities for sustainable growth," Lee said.
PMCK remains supportive of public-private healthcare collaboration and will monitor developments under the Health Ministry's Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme.
It will also continue to evaluate potential mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures and strategic partnerships that complement its existing operations.
PMC Kulim remains a key component of PMCK's growth strategy.

Title: Understand legal channels, seek accurate guidance - Raja Muda of Perlis
Article:
PADANG BESAR: Every citizen should be aware of their rights and responsibilities by understanding available legal channels and seeking accurate guidance when requiring related services.
The Raja Muda of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, said the Legal Aid Department plays a vital role as a bridge between the community and the justice system.
"The services help the public understand their rights, get guidance, and choose appropriate resolution channels," His Highness said when officiating the closing ceremony of the Perlis state-level Legal Aid Department Discourse "Yang Jauh Didekati, Yang Sulit Disantuni" 2026 at Felda Rimba Mas today.
At the event, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra also witnessed the signing of a Note of Cooperation between the department and the Perlis Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIPs).
Meanwhile, the Raja Muda of Perlis said the discourse exposed participants to the latest service developments, including expanded legal aid in civil and Syariah matters, the Madani Mediation Centre, Legal Companion, and Public Defence.
His Highness said these knowledge-sharing initiatives should expand to ensure legal awareness reaches a broader segment of society.
"Every participant can act as a bridge to help those around them recognise their rights, understand available channels, and access legal services more easily," His Highness added.
On the Note of Cooperation, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said the collaboration reflects both institutions' commitment to extending service benefits to the community, especially the asnaf group.

Title: Inta Bina lands RM221mil Klang job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Inta Bina Group Bhd has clinched a RM221.08 million contract from Prisma Melody Sdn Bhd, for the main building works of Gravit8 Phase 4 (Novva) in Kota Bayuemas, Klang, Selangor.
Prisma Melody is a wholly owned subsidiary of Mitraland Holding (M) Sdn Bhd.
Inta Bina said it is the fourth project the company has undertaken with Mitraland, extending a business relationship that has spanned 14 years.
It raises Inta Bina's new order book to about RM645 million from about RM424 million, providing greater earnings visibility as the construction group replenishes its project pipeline.
The development comprises a 39-storey serviced apartment tower with 654 units and a 20-storey office tower, along with parking facilities, commercial spaces, recreational facilities and a sports complex.
Construction is scheduled to begin on Sept 28.
The works are divided into two sections, with Section 1 having a 24-month contract period and targeted for completion by Sept 27, 2028.
Section 2 has a 28-month contract period and is scheduled for completion by Jan 27, 2029.
Inta Bina managing director Paul Lim said the company valued Mitraland's continued confidence and looked forward to delivering the project on time.
Lim said Inta Bina maintained a healthy tender book of about RM3.6 billion, comprising residential, commercial and data centre projects.
Inta Bina said the latest award underscored its focus on securing projects while building long-term relationships with established property developers.

Title: Fire at Poland Starlink station 'sabotage', says minister
Article:
WARSAW: A fire broke out at a Starlink satellite communications station in central Poland overnight, the digital affairs minister said on Thursday, calling the blaze an act of "sabotage."
"This act of sabotage was deliberately designed to disable the station ... disrupting internet access for various institutions, including the Ukrainian army," Krzysztof Gawkowski told Polish public broadcaster TVP Info, adding that the fire broke out late on Wednesday and that the station was still operational.
"There is much to suggest that we are dealing with an element of the next phase of hybrid warfare," he added.
The station, owned by state-owned telecommunications company Exatel, is used, among other things, to transmit internet traffic through Poland, including to Ukraine, according to the minister.
It is also used by SpaceX systems that provide connectivity via Starlink terminals.
Gawkowski said that the investigation was ongoing into the causes of the blaze, "many indications suggest that it fits into this new Russian doctrine of attack."
Poland, a NATO and EU member state along the alliance's eastern flank, has accused Russia of "sabotage" on several occasions since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Poland has become the main hub for transporting Western military and humanitarian support to Kyiv.
Earlier this month, Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Russia's plans in the war against Ukraine include "hybrid" drone and missile strikes against Kyiv's allies.

Title: MACC and FBI reinforce cooperation to tackle corruption, cross-border crimes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) are reinforcing their cooperation through the exchange of experience and expertise, as well as capacity-building in enforcement.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was among the matters discussed during a courtesy visit by an FBI delegation led by Law Enforcement Attaché Varinder Singh to the MACC headquarters today.
"Strategic cooperation with the FBI is an important platform for strengthening enforcement capabilities through the sharing of experience, expertise, and best practices, besides benefiting the capacity-building of MACC officers," he said in a statement today.
Halim said the nearly hour-long meeting focused on operational issues, including corruption linked to fraudulent activities and coordination between enforcement agencies in addressing cross-border crime challenges.
He said the visit also opened up opportunities for both sides to explore new areas of cooperation that could be strengthened in the future.
"The opportunity to participate in various programmes and training conducted by the FBI is invaluable," he said.
Also present were MACC senior directors Datuk Y.S. Karunanithy (Special Operations Division), Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin (Intelligence Division), and director Datuk Saiful Hazmi Mohd Saad (Legal and Prosecution Division), as well as FBI Assistant Law Enforcement Attaché Cody Kirk.

Title: Infomina bags RM62.7mil tech contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Infomina Bhd has secured a RM62.65 million contract from a local financial institution to provide technology refresh, supply and maintenance services over 69 months.
Infomina will provide technology refresh and maintenance services covering the supply, delivery, installation, configuration, integration, testing, commissioning and implementation of hardware, equipment, software and related items.
The scope also includes ongoing support and maintenance services throughout the contract period.
Infomina chief executive officer-cum-managing director Yee Chee Meng said the contract reflected continued confidence in its ability to support critical technology environments.
"Long-term maintenance and support engagements remain an important part of our business model, providing recurring revenue while allowing us to build deeper and longer-lasting relationships with our customers," he said.
Yee said Infomina will work with the financial institution to ensure its technology infrastructure remained reliable, resilient and well supported throughout the contract period.
The company said the contract also supported its efforts to expand its recurring operations, maintenance and support services alongside its technology infrastructure and enterprise solutions businesses.
As organisations modernise their technology environments to meet growing digitalisation needs, Infomina said it continued to see opportunities to help enterprises and institutions refresh, optimise and maintain their critical technology infrastructure.
The company said it will continue to pursue opportunities across the public and private sectors, leveraging its capabilities in mission-critical infrastructure, cloud, data, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and managed services.

Title: Former Petronas manager met Petros official informally before interview - Witness
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Sessions Court today heard that former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal Mohd Jasni met informally with a senior official of Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) at the Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC), before a formal interview for a position at the company in 2024.
The fifth prosecution witness, a former Petronas employee, said the meeting took place before Mohd Khairul Akmal's interview with Petros chief financial officer and chief executive officer, Mohd Azha Abdul Jalil and Datuk Janin Girie, respectively, at the company's office in Kuching, Sarawak.
"He met Mohd Azha at the KLGCC before the formal interview, but I am not sure of the date," the witness said during examination-in-chief by deputy public prosecutor Noor Syafina Mohd Radzuan in the trial of Khairul Akmal, who faces a charge of attempting to disclose a report to Petros in June 2024.
The witness said Khairul Akmal applied for the position of Head of Upstream Finance at Petros in 2024, while he was Manager of Business Planning Performance Review Upstream at Petronas.
When questioned by Noor Syafina whether the two positions were similar in terms of scope of duties, the witness replied, "There are similarities".
Noor Syafina
: To your knowledge, do you know the salary scale for this position at Petros?
Witness
: I don't quite remember, but he asked me how much he should request, and I gave him some advice. I suggested how much he should ask from Petros at the time.
However, the witness, whose name is withheld under the law, did not remember the suggestion given at the time.
The witness, who served with Petronas for 12 years, said that under the Petronas Code of Ethics, employees of the company must obtain prior approval before sharing any sensitive information, such as emails relating to the company.
"If you are referring to the sharing of sensitive company information, approval must first be obtained from the parties involved. As employees, we cannot share confidential and sensitive information without approval," the witness said.
Khairul Akmal, 41, is accused of attempting to disclose information, namely, a document titled "Q1 2024 Upstream Business Performance Operational & Financial", to Petros at a condominium in Jalan Pinang, between 3.19pm and 3.21pm on June 8, 2024.
He had allegedly obtained the document while serving as Manager of Business Performance for a Petronas business unit.
The charge is framed under Section 203A(1) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 511 of the same Code, which provides for a maximum fine of RM1 million or jail of up to one year.
However, Section 511 caps any custodial sentence at half that term upon conviction.
Section 511 carries a sentence of jail not exceeding half of that under Section 203A(1), upon conviction.
The trial before Judge Mazuliana Abdul Rashid resumes tomorrow.

Title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, eases versus US dollar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:The ringgit ended higher against major currencies on Thursday but weakened against the greenback as upbeat United States economic data reinforced expectations of further interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve (Fed).
At 6pm, the ringgit decreased to 4.0840/0880 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0780/0825.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit experienced volatile trading against the US dollar, weakening to RM4.0940 during the morning session before regaining strength to RM4.0793 in the afternoon.
"The recovery happened even though the US dollar remained strong, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) staying at around 101 points," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies.
It gained against the euro to 4.6451/6497 from 4.6522/6573 at Wednesday's close and advanced vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.4023/4076 from 5.4156/4216. It also strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5723/5750 from 2.5836/5868 previously.
The local note also traded mostly higher against its Asean peers.
It slightly increased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1906/1940 from 3.1909/1947 at Wednesday's close and strengthened versus the Thai baht to 12.1950/2121 from 12.2599/2782.
The ringgit also advanced against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.9/228.2 from 228.8/229.2 and remained unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.51/6.52.

Title: Experts call for skid tests after multiple riders fall on green-painted lane
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Road safety experts are calling for skid-resistance tests on the green-painted stretch of the Federal Highway motorcycle lane near Subang after a viral video showed multiple riders falling on the rain-soaked surface.
While they emphasise that coloured road surfacing is not inherently unsafe, questions remain over whether the coating used at the location provides sufficient traction under wet conditions.
The call comes after a
42-second clip posted
on Threads showed several motorcycles lying on the rain-slicked green lane.
Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research chairman Professor Dr Wong Shaw Voon told the New Straits Times he believed the painted surface was applied for a reason, suggesting the coating was likely intended to warn riders of an accident-prone zone.
"It doesn't mean that having painted road surfaces is not good," Wong said, adding that engineering interventions could produce coloured surfaces with even better skid-resistant properties than regular asphalt.
He said repeated incidents at the same location warranted serious attention, and that further inspection and testing were needed.
"We need to test the skid resistance on both dry and wet surfaces," he said.
He noted that a road's grip could decline over time as its surface becomes 'polished', and warned riders against assuming that a newly painted surface allowed them to travel faster.
"You cannot say, 'Now I'm on a new road, so I can drive fast'," he said, adding that taking a bend at high speeds causes a loss of grip regardless of surface quality, and regaining control is difficult once that happens.
He noted that many small motorcycles lack anti-lock braking systems (ABS), increasing the risk of wheel lock when braking while cornering.
"The best way, of course, for the public, for the riders, is to always reduce speed," he said.
Universiti Putra Malaysia Road Safety Research Centre head Associate Professor Dr Law Teik Hua said the video alone was not enough to prove the paint caused the falls.
"However, there does appear to be a legitimate safety concern regarding repeated loss-of-control incidents among multiple motorcycles traversing the wet pavement section," he told the New Straits Times.
He recommended a technical inquiry to assess whether the painted surface was slip-resistant enough under wet conditions, particularly during braking, acceleration or turning.
He said friction on the painted surface and adjacent bare asphalt should be measured and compared under wet conditions, along with factors such as drainage, surface texture, contamination, tyre condition, speed and rider paths.
"Research suggests that macrotexture is highly significant for wet performance since the texture allows effective drainage at the tyre-pavement contact patch.
"If the colour application shows significantly poorer wet friction performance compared to asphalt, the treatment area should not be applied at the bends.
"Alternatively, the application design could be revised to ensure satisfactory wet friction performance," he said.
Following the incident, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the Public Works Department was examining the site to determine why the riders had lost control at that section.
He said the road was designed to be
skid-resistant
and promised swift remedial action.
The motorcycle lane where the crashes occurred will be resurfaced and fitted with a
40kph speed
sign as an immediate mitigation measure.

Title: Starbucks to close another 250 coffeehouses in North America
Article:
NEW YORK: Starbucks will close 250 underperforming coffeehouses in North America, the company said in a regulatory filing on Thursday, as chief executive officer (CEO) Brian Niccol deepens his turnaround push to revive sales.
The closures come a year after Starbucks shut down several underperforming stores in the region, including its iconic Seattle roastery, in a restructuring effort that was estimated to cost the company about US$1 billion.
The company disclosed on Thursday that the fresh closures will result in about US$300 million in restructuring charges and represent about one per cent of its roughly 18,000 stores in North America.
It plans to finish most of the closures by the end of fiscal year 2026.
Starbucks also expects fiscal 2026 global net new store openings for company-operated and licensed coffeehouses to be about 440, compared with its earlier target of 600 to 650 openings.
Niccol completed two years as CEO of Starbucks in September.
The former Chipotle Mexican Grill executive has tried to draw back customers with shorter wait times and simpler menus in the United States as part of his "Back to Starbucks" plan.
Starbucks also invested in store and kitchen operations, and has tried to manage costs by cutting several corporate roles and shutting down some regional offices.
As of July this year, the company had reported four straight quarters of comparable sales growth.
ustomer traffic increased across all income cohorts, Niccol said in April.
The company has also refreshed its loyalty programme and add-ons such as protein cold foam, helping drive sales.
Its pricey lattes have resisted a broader slowdown in non-essential spending, particularly among lower-income consumers in the United States as households buckle under high costs of fuel and food.

Title: Honda gives City a tech-driven refresh
Article:
HONDA Malaysia has launched the new City with sharper styling, upgraded technology and enhanced safety features as it seeks to keep one of its longest-running nameplates relevant to changing urban driving needs.
The refreshed sedan, marking 24 years of the City in Malaysia, comes in four variants - E, V, Petrol RS and e:HEV RS - priced from RM89,900 to RM111,900, excluding insurance.
More than 536,000 City units have been sold in Malaysia since its introduction, while its hybrid variant accounts for about 22 per cent of Honda Malaysia's total hybrid sales.
Honda Malaysia managing director and chief executive officer Narushi Yazaki said the latest iteration was designed to offer a sportier appearance and greater convenience while retaining the model's practicality, performance and efficiency.
"For more than two decades, the City has established a strong presence in Malaysia, becoming part of the everyday lives of Malaysians," he said.
The new City gets a redesigned front grille, new long light bar headlights for RS variants and Bi-LED headlights as standard across the range.
The exterior is complemented by new 16-inch dual-tone milling alloy wheels, while the cabin receives a larger 10-inch display audio system.
The e:HEV RS also gets a wireless charger, while new ambient lighting, footlight and door-pocket illumination add to the cabin's functionality.
The model retains its 1.5-litre petrol powertrain, producing 121 PS and 145 Nm of torque, paired with a continuously variable transmission.
The e:HEV RS delivers maximum torque of 253 Nm through Honda's hybrid system, which manages the petrol engine and electric motors according to driving conditions.
Honda Sensing remains standard across all variants, while the City now adds blind spot information with cross traffic monitoring across the range.
Honda LaneWatch is also standard, while petrol RS and e:HEV RS variants gain a 360-degree multi-view camera system to improve visibility when parking and manoeuvring.
The e:HEV RS comes with Honda Malaysia's 10-year hybrid battery warranty with unlimited mileage.
The City 1.5L E is priced at RM89,900, followed by the V at RM94,900, the petrol RS at RM99,900 and the e:HEV RS at RM111,900.
Available colours are Platinum White Pearl, Meteoroid Gray Metallic, Stellar Diamond Pearl and the new Blazing Red Pearl.
To mark the City's 24th anniversary in Malaysia, Honda Malaysia is offering a special City reward programme for the first 2,400 eligible customers.
The company has also extended its warranty coverage to up to eight years with unlimited mileage for newly purchased Honda petrol and hybrid models from Sept 1.

Title: SLGC IPO oversubscribed 3.1 times ahead of ACE Market listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SLGC Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) has been oversubscribed by 3.1 times, ahead of its listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia Securities.
In a statement today, the building construction services provider said the public portion was oversubscribed by 4.9 times, while the Bumiputera portion was oversubscribed by 1.2 times.
For the Malaysian public portion, which comprises 28 million new shares, SLGC received 4,647 applications for 113.70 million shares valued at RM31.8 million.
Of these, the Bumiputera portion received 1,962 applications for 31.30 million shares, while the public portion received 2,685 applications for 82.39 million shares.
SLGC said the two million shares allocated to eligible directors and employees under the Pink Form Allocations have been fully subscribed.
Meanwhile, the 70.0 million new shares reserved for private placement to Bumiputera investors approved by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry, as well as 5.0 million new shares and 63.0 million offer shares reserved for selected investors, including institutional shareholders, have also been fully placed.
The allotment and transfer of the IPO shares to successful applicants are scheduled for Oct 2, with the company scheduled to list on Oct 6.
SLGC said the IPO comprises a public issue of 105 million new ordinary shares at an issue price of 28 sen per share, representing 18.8 per cent of its enlarged issued share capital, raising gross proceeds of RM29.4 million.
Managing director Yong Zhen Lin said the encouraging response reflected investors' confidence in the group's track record, project execution capabilities and growth prospects.
"Looking ahead, we remain positive on the opportunities available to the group, particularly in the industrial segment," he said.
Yong said continued investments in manufacturing plants, warehouses, logistics facilities, data centres and other industrial developments are expected to support demand for construction services.
He also said the company is selectively tendering for new projects while maintaining disciplined project execution and building its project pipeline.
The group, through its subsidiaries, provides building construction services, including design-and-build, external and ancillary works, primarily as a main contractor for commercial, industrial and residential developments.
As at Aug 12, 2026, SLGC had an unbilled order book of RM1.0 billion that would be recognised progressively over the next five financial years.
From the RM29.4 million IPO proceeds, RM9.2 million will be used to purchase construction machinery and equipment, RM7.6 million to repay bank borrowings, RM7.5 million for working capital and RM500,000 to upgrade construction management software.
The remaining RM4.6 million has been earmarked for estimated listing expenses.
Upon listing, SLGC is expected to have a market capitalisation of approximately RM156.8 million based on the IPO price of 28 sen and enlarged issued share capital of 560 million shares.
M&A Securities Sdn Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO exercise.

Title: Foreign funds return, but rotation points to caution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign investors returned to Malaysian equities last week but the modest inflow masked a broader rotation away from rate-sensitive sectors and towards more defensive counters, according to Moomoo Malaysia.
Foreign institutions were net buyers of RM127 million of Malaysian equities, ending six consecutive weeks of net selling.
The inflow came after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to four per cent, its first hike since 2023, amid persistent US inflation and an energy shock linked to the war with Iran.
Moomoo Malaysia said the sector breakdown suggested investors were repositioning rather than broadly increasing exposure to Malaysian stocks.
Financial services recorded the largest foreign outflow at RM309.7 million, followed by plantations at RM131.1 million, utilities at RM84.5 million and healthcare at RM84 million.
"Foreign selling was concentrated in financial services, the most foreign-owned and liquid segment of the market and one that reacts quickly to rates and currency movements," Moomoo Malaysia said.
It noted that plantation stocks, whose earnings are largely US dollar-linked, could benefit from a weaker ringgit following a more hawkish Fed stance.
The three sectors attracting the most foreign funds accounted for RM299.6 million, while the three biggest outflow sectors recorded RM439.7 million in selling.
This points to more than RM700 million in identifiable two-way foreign activity despite the relatively small net inflow.
Foreign average daily trading value also jumped 41.3 per cent week-on-week, suggesting investors were actively repositioning rather than simply returning to the market.
Meanwhile, local institutions remained net sellers at RM368 million, extending their selling streak to two weeks.
Retail investors were net buyers of RM241 million, marking their fourth consecutive week of buying.
Moomoo Malaysia said investors should focus on the composition of foreign flows rather than the headline figure in coming weeks.
"A repeat would suggest overseas investors are deliberately lowering exposure to rates and the ringgit rather than reacting to a single week," it said.
It also urged investors to monitor the ringgit, US yields and Fed policy signals, while watching whether retail buying continues to offset institutional selling.
Foreign ownership of Malaysian equities fell to about 18 per cent last month, a record low.
This highlighted that the latest inflow remains a relatively small shift in the broader positioning of overseas investors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ICT Zone's Q2 earnings up 11pct on lower expenses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ICT Zone Asia Bhd's net profit rose 11 per cent in the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2 FY27), supported by lower operating expenses.
The net profit for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 rose to RM4.25 million from RM3.8 million a year ago, while revenue jumped 40 per cent to RM71.9 million from RM51 million.
The company declared a dividend of 0.22 sen per share, payable on Nov 3.
For the first half of FY27, ICT Zone's net profit rose 22 per cent to RM8.7 million from RM7 million, supported by an 85 per cent jump in revenue to RM172 million from RM92.9 million.
In a statement, ICT Zone said its unbilled order book reached RM313.45 million as at end-July, surpassing a key threshold.
This represented an 11.7 per cent increase from RM280.66 million at end-April 2026, indicating that new contract wins were outpacing ongoing billings.
ICT Zone managing director and chief executive officer Tommy Lim Kok Kwang said the company's technology financing business continued to grow during the quarter, translating into a larger contracted base for it.
"The increase in our unbilled order book from RM280.7 million to RM313.5 million over the past three months gives us greater visibility of increased revenue to be recognised in the coming years.
The company continues to execute its circular-economy strategy by remarketing and leasing refurbished ICT assets once they complete their initial financing lifecycles.
This extends the useful life of the assets and broadens market access to cost-effective technology solutions.
ICT Zone remains cautiously optimistic about its outlook for the remainder of the financial year.
"Growth is expected to be supported by the shift among corporates from capital expenditure, where technology is purchased upfront, to operating expenditure, where technology is paid for as an ongoing service.
"It will also be supported by growing adoption of AI-capable enterprise devices, scheduled hardware refresh cycles and collaborations such as the MDEC Business Digitalisation Initiative," the company said.

Title: LB Group invests RM1bil in Kedah plant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: LB Group Co Ltd, a global titanium dioxide (TiO₂) and advanced inorganic chemicals producer, has broken ground on a RM1 billion manufacturing facility in Gurun, Kedah, as part of its expansion in Southeast Asia.
The project, undertaken through its Malaysian subsidiary LB Advanced Material Asia Sdn Bhd, will be developed on 24.3 hectares at the Gurun Heavy Industrial Park.
Phase one involves an investment of RM600 million, with the facility expected to reach an annual production capacity of 300,000 tonnes upon completion.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chief executive officer Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid said the investment reflects confidence in Malaysia's industrial ecosystem and its potential as a regional manufacturing hub.
He said the project would strengthen the country's capabilities in high-value manufacturing and contribute to the development of a more complex and resilient chemical industry.
This is in line with the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and Chemical Industry Roadmap 2030.
Malaysia's strategic advantages, robust heavy industrial infrastructure and welcoming investment environment were key factors behind the investment, LB Advanced Material Asia director Liang Sun said.
He said the Gurun facility's access to major highway and rail networks, as well as connectivity to Penang Port, would support export efficiency and enable the group to better serve regional and global customers.
LB Group operates an integrated value chain covering titanium minerals, TiO₂ and titanium sponge, as well aszirconium products and new energy materials.
Its BILLIONS brand serves more than 1,500 customers globally across applications including coatings, plastics, inks and paper.
The Malaysian project is expected to create more than 300 skilled jobs while supporting the development of Kedah's industrial and chemical manufacturing ecosystem.

Title: Nine areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nine areas nationwide registered unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 6pm today, according to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
The readings were recorded in Sarawak, with Serian recording the country's worst air quality at 194.
Eight other stations in the state also recorded unhealthy air quality levels. These were the state capital, Kuching, at 187, followed by Samarahan (175), Sri Aman (173), Bintulu (159), Sarikei (157), Sibu (155), Samalaju (153) and Kapit (144).
Meanwhile, 47 monitoring stations across the country recorded moderate air quality.
Among them were Mukah in Sarawak at 94, followed by Bukit Rambai in Melaka at 92. Cheras in Kuala Lumpur, Shah Alam in Selangor and Labuan each recorded an API reading of 86.
Other areas included Nilai (83), Seremban (82), Pasir Gudang (81), Miri (81) and Johan Setia (81).
As for good air quality levels, Minden, Balik Pulau and Temerloh led at 49 each. Other areas with good readings included Paka and Kuala Terengganu (48 each), Kota Baru (47), Alor Star (43), Jerantut (42), Tanah Merah (29), Besut (23), Kangar (22) and Langkawi (21).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous.

Title: PM's elder brother Idrus Ibrahim dies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed his grief over the death of his elder brother Idrus Ibrahim today.
"On my way back to Malaysia, I received the heartbreaking news that my brother, Idrus Ibrahim, has died.
"It is difficult for me to put into words the sense of loss I feel when someone who shared so many memories throughout my life is now gone. Only Allah knows how heavy my heart feels as I accept this reality.
"I regret not being able to be by his side in his final moments, but I accept this with an open heart, even as I am still trying to come to terms with a separation we were never prepared to face," he said in a Facebook post.

Title: Traffic cop suffers broken arm, leg after driver rams roadblock
Article:
IPOH: A traffic policeman suffered a broken arm and leg after being rammed by a driver who tried to evade a roadblock inspection on Jalan Silibin, here, this morning.
Ipoh police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police managed to arrest the 29-year-old man after his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction.
He said the incident happened about 9.45am when a traffic policeman ordered the car to stop, but the driver failed to comply with the instruction and sped away.
Three other personnel who were there pursued the car. Upon arriving at the traffic light area near the Perak State Secretariat (SUK) Building, the driver entered the left lane before making a sudden U-turn and rammed into a traffic policeman.
"The driver then fled towards Gunung Lang, and upon reaching the area near McDonald's Gunung Lang, the driver drove against the flow of traffic before his car skidded at the Taman Wing Onn traffic light junction," Najib said in a statement today.
He said that as a result of the incident, the traffic personnel suffered a fractured left arm and right leg and was taken to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB) for further treatment.
He added that further investigations on the male driver revealed that the suspect did not possess a driver's licence, the vehicle's road tax had expired, and an initial urine screening test on the suspect came back positive for methamphetamine.
The case is being investigated under Section 44(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless driving.
Earlier, an 18-second video went viral on social media showing a white vehicle moving at high speed, hitting a road divider, driving against the flow of traffic, and crashing into several vehicles on Jalan Kuala Kangsar, Ipoh. -- BERNAMA

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends lower on rising oil prices, elevated bond yields
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended lower on Thursday, weighed down by moderate selling pressure interspersed with buying activity as renewed hikes in oil prices and elevated global bond yields dampened investor sentiment, said an analyst.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 4.12 points, or 0.24 per cent, to 1,672.31, from Wednesday's close of 1,676.43.
The benchmark index, which opened 1.98 points lower at 1,674.45, moved between 1,671.48 and 1,679.47 during the day.
Market breadth was also negative, with losers outpacing gainers 677 to 436, while 542 counters were unchanged, 1,246 untraded and 27 suspended.
Turnover widened to 3.32 billion units worth RM2.74 billion from 3.20 billion units valued at RM2.99 billion on Wednesday.
IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said benchmark Brent crude futures for November jumped as much as 3.3 per cent to US$106.50 per barrel before paring some gains.
He said the rise in oil prices added to concerns that higher energy costs could reinforce inflationary pressures and keep interest rates higher for longer.
"Regionally, equities also came under pressure as bond yields remained near two-decade highs, weighing on equity valuations," he said.
For Bursa Malaysia, Mohd Sedek said, the combination of higher oil prices, elevated yields and persistent foreign selling is likely to keep risk appetite cautious, while investors may continue to favour defensive and commodity-linked sectors.
At the time of writing, Brent crude oil climbed 2.45 per cent to US$105.54 per barrel.

Title: UUE wins RM29.8mil jobs in Singapore
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: UUE Holdings Bhd has secured four contracts worth a combined S$9.3 million (RM29.8 million) in Singapore, bringing its financial year-to-date contract wins to RM127.9 million.
In a statement, the underground utilities engineering solutions provider said its subsidiary, Konnection Engineering Pte Ltd, secured the contracts from Hong Kong-listed Wee Guan Group.
They cover supplying and installing 400kV power cables, auxiliary cables and related accessories.
The latest jobs are expected to strengthen UUE's order book and provide earnings visibility for the next two to three years.
Across the four subcontracts, SP PowerAssets Ltd is the principal, with Konnection responsible for supplying the necessary materials and labour for horizontal directional drilling works to install high-density polyethylene pipes, in accordance with SP PowerAssets' contract specifications.
The projects are expected to be completed by December 2028.
UUE managing director Datuk Dr Ting Kok Hwa said the contracts strengthen the company's presence in Singapore and Malaysia.
"These four subcontracts reinforce UUE's position as an underground utilities engineering solutions provider in both Malaysia and Singapore," he said.
Ting said the 400kV transmission network in Singapore required high standards of technical precision, safety and operational execution.
He added that the awards validated UUE's ability to meet Singapore's stringent national utility standards.
"We remain committed to delivering these critical infrastructure projects safely, reliably and on schedule," he said.
Ting said UUE would continue leveraging its growing order book across Malaysia and Singapore to support sustainable growth and create value for shareholders.
